translations.text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,
which he promised beforehand through his prophets in the holy Scriptures,
concerning his Son, who was descended from David according to the flesh,
designated the Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness through the resurrection of the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,
through whom we received grace and apostleship to bring about the obedience of faith among all the nations for his name,
among whom you too are called to belong to Jesus Christ.
To all of you who are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: grace to you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.
God, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, is my witness to how I remember you
at all times in my prayers, asking that perhaps at last, by God's will, I may succeed in coming to you.
For I long to see you, so that I may impart some spiritual gift to you to strengthen you,
that is, to be encouraged together with you through our mutual faith, both mine and yours.
I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that I have often intended to come to you, but have been prevented until now, so that I might obtain some fruit among you as among the other nations.
For I am a debtor to Greeks and barbarians, to the wise and the foolish.
So, as far as it lies with me, I am eager to preach the gospel to you who are in Rome as well.
For I do not consider the gospel anything to be ashamed of, because it is the power of God for the salvation of everyone who believes, first the Jew and then the Gentile.
For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith, as it is written: "The righteous person will live by faith."
For the wrath of God will be revealed from heaven against all the ungodliness and unrighteousness of people who hold back the truth through unrighteousness,
because the knowledge of God is evident in them, for God himself made it evident to them.
For since the beginning of the world, his invisible attributes are understood and seen through created things—that is, his eternity, power, and divinity—so that they can offer no defense at all.
For they knew God but did not glorify him as God or give thanks. Instead, their thoughts became futile, and their hearts were darkened by foolishness.
They considered themselves wise but became fools.
And they exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of a corruptible human being, and of birds, four-footed animals, and reptiles.
Therefore God gave them over, in the desires of their hearts, to impurity, to dishonor their bodies among themselves.
They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and obeyed and worshiped created things rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
For this reason God handed them over to shameful passions, for their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.

Likewise, the men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with desire for one another. Men committed shameful acts with men and received in themselves the repayment that their error deserved.
And since they did not choose to retain the knowledge of God, God handed them over to a dishonorable mind, to do things that are unworthy.
They were filled with every kind of injustice, sexual immorality, wickedness, greed, and evil, full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice; they were whisperers,
slanderers, haters of God, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil, disrespectful to their parents,
foolish, breakers of agreements, without natural affection, irreconcilable, and merciless.
They knew God's decree that those who do such things deserve death—not only those who do them, but also those who approve of those who practice them.
Therefore you have no excuse, whoever you are who judge, for in judging another you condemn yourself, because you do the same things for which you judge.
For we know that God's judgment against those who do such things is in accordance with the truth.
Now do you think, whoever you are who judge those who do such things while doing the same things yourself, that you will escape God's judgment?
Or do you despise the abundance of his kindness, forbearance, and patience? Do you not know that God's kindness leads you to repentance?
But because of your stubbornness and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and the revelation of God's righteous judgment,
who will repay each person according to their deeds:
eternal life to those who persevere in doing good and seek glory, honor, and immortality;
but wrath and anger to those who are contentious, rebel against the truth, and follow injustice.
There will be affliction and distress for every person who does evil, first the Jew and then the Gentile,
but glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good, first the Jew and then the Gentile.
For there is no partiality with God.
All who sinned outside the law will also perish outside the law, and those who sinned under the law will also be judged by the law.
For it is not the hearers of the law who are justified before God, but the doers of the law who will be justified.
But when Gentiles who do not have the law do by nature what the law requires, they, though they do not have the law, are a law to themselves.
They show that the work of the law is written in their hearts, with their consciences bearing witness and their thoughts accusing one another or even offering a defense,
on the day when God judges people's secrets through Jesus Christ, according to my gospel.
But if you are called a Jew, rely on the law, and boast in God,
and know his will and discern what is best, having been instructed by the law,
you are confident that you yourself are a guide to the blind, a light to those in darkness,
An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of children, having in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth.
You, then, who teach your neighbor, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
You who say not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who detest pagan temples, do you plunder altars?
You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
For God's name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you, just as it is written.
Circumcision is beneficial if you keep the law. But if you are a lawbreaker, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
But if an uncircumcised person keeps the requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be counted as circumcision?
And the person who is uncircumcised by nature, by fulfilling the law, will judge you who, despite having the written law and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.
For a Jew is not someone who is one outwardly, nor is circumcision something outward in the flesh.
Rather, a Jew is someone who is one inwardly, and circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit and not by the written law. Such a person's praise comes not from people but from God.
What advantage, then, does the Jew have, or what benefit is there in circumcision?
Much in every way. First of all, they were entrusted with the words of God.
What, then, if some did not believe? Would their unbelief nullify God's faithfulness? Certainly not!
Let God be truthful and every person a liar, just as it is written: “So that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged.”
But now, if our unrighteousness demonstrates God's righteousness, what shall we say? Is God unjust when he brings wrath upon us?
I speak in human terms. Certainly not! Otherwise, how will God judge the world?
For if God's truth has increased through my lie to his glory, why am I still judged as a sinner?
Or why not say, as we are slanderously accused and as some claim we say, “Let us do evil so that good may come”? Their condemnation is just.
What, then? Are we better in any way? Certainly not in any way, for we have already charged both Jews and Gentiles with all being under sin.
Just as it is written: “There is no one righteous, not even one.
There is no one who understands, and no one who seeks God.
All have turned aside; together they have become useless. There is no one who does good, not even one.
Their throat is an open grave; with their tongues they have practiced deceit. The venom of vipers is under their lips.
Their mouths are full of curses and bitterness.
Their feet are swift to shed blood.
Destruction and misery are in their paths.
And they have not known the way of peace.
There is no fear of God before their eyes.”
But we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world may stand condemned before God.
For no one will be justified before him by works of the law, because through the law comes knowledge of sin.
But now the righteousness of God has been revealed apart from the law, with the law and the prophets bearing witness to it.
For the righteousness of God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe, and there is no distinction.
For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
And they are justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
God put him forward as an atonement through faith in his blood, to demonstrate his righteousness because of the forgiveness of sins previously committed in God's forbearance.
This was to demonstrate his righteousness at the present time, so that he might be just and justify the one who has faith in Jesus.
Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. By what law? By a law of works? No, but by the law of faith.
For we consider that a person is justified by faith apart from works of the law.
Is God the God of the Jews only, and not of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles too.
For if God is one, who justifies the circumcised through faith, then he also justifies the uncircumcised through that same faith.
Do we then nullify the law through this faith? Certainly not! Rather, we uphold the law.
What, then, shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, discovered?
For if Abraham was justified by works, he had grounds for boasting, but not before God.
For what does Scripture say? Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
Now to the one who works, wages are counted not as a gift but as a debt.
But to the one who does not work but believes in the one who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness.
David likewise speaks of the blessedness of the person to whom God counts righteousness apart from works:
Blessed are those whose lawless deeds have been forgiven and whose sins have been covered.
Blessed is the man whose sins the Lord will not count against him.
Is this blessedness, then, for the circumcised or also for the uncircumcised? For we say that Abraham's faith was counted as righteousness.
How, then, was it counted? While he was circumcised or uncircumcised? Not while circumcised, but while uncircumcised.

And he received circumcision as a sign, a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had while uncircumcised, so that he might be the father of all who believe while uncircumcised, so that righteousness might be counted to them too.
And he is the father of the circumcised who are not merely circumcised but also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had while uncircumcised.
For the promises to Abraham and his offspring that he would inherit the world did not come through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
For if those who belong to the law are heirs, then faith is useless and the promises are empty.
For the law brings about wrath, but where there is no law, there is no transgression either.

Therefore it comes through faith, so that it may be according to grace and the promises may be secure for all the offspring—not only those who belong to the law, but also those who share Abraham’s faith. He is the father of us all,
as it is written: “I have made you the father of many nations”—in the presence of God, in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls what does not exist as though it exists.
Against all hope, he believed with hope that he would become the father of many nations, as he had been told: “So shall your offspring be.”
He did not waver in faith, even though he considered his own body as already dead, since he was about a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah’s womb.
But he did not doubt God’s promises through unbelief; instead, he grew strong in faith and gave glory to God,
and became firmly convinced in his mind that the one who had promised was able to do it.
Therefore it was credited to him as righteousness.
Now the words “it was credited to him” were not written for his sake alone,
but also for ours. It will be credited to us who believe in the one who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,
who was handed over because of our offenses and was raised to make us righteous.
Therefore, having been made righteous through faith, let us have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
through whom we have also gained access by faith to this grace in which we stand, and we boast in the hope of God’s glory.
And not only that, but we also boast in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces endurance,
endurance produces proven character, and proven character produces hope.
Hope never puts us to shame, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.
For while we were still weak, Christ died for us at the proper time, on behalf of the ungodly.
For someone will scarcely die for a righteous person, though perhaps someone might dare to die for a good person.
God showed his love for us in that, while we were still sinners,
Christ died for us. How much more, now that we have been made righteous by his blood, will we be saved through him from wrath!
For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, how much more, now that we have been reconciled, will we be saved by his life!
And not only that, but we also boast in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.
For just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so death spread to all people, because all sinned.
For sin was in the world before the law, but sin is not counted where there is no law.
Yet death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over those who had not sinned in the same way as Adam’s transgression. Adam is a type of the one to come.

But the gift of grace is not like the trespass. For if many died through the trespass of one man, how much more did the grace of God and the gift through the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, overflow to many.
And the gift is not like the result of one man's sin. For the judgment arising from one trespass led to condemnation, but the gift of grace arising from many trespasses led to justification.

For if, through the trespass of one man, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ.
So then, just as one man's trespass brought condemnation to all people, so also one man's righteousness brought justification and life to all people.
For just as through the disobedience of one man many became sinners, so also through the obedience of one man many will become righteous.
But the law came in so that trespasses might multiply. And where sin increased, grace increased still more.
So that, just as sin reigned in death, grace might also reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may multiply?
Certainly not! How can we who died to sin still live in it?
Or do you not know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?
We were buried with him through baptism into death, so that, just as Christ rose from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life.
For if we have been united with him in the likeness of his death, we shall also be united with him in his resurrection.
Know this: our old self was crucified with him so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, and we might no longer serve sin.
For the one who has died has been freed from sin.
But if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him.
We know that Christ, having risen from the dead, no longer dies, and death no longer rules over him.
For the death he died, he died to sin once, and the life he lives, he lives to God.
Likewise, you too must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Therefore, do not let sin reign in your mortal bodies, making you obey their desires.

And do not offer the parts of your bodies to sin as weapons of unrighteousness. Instead, offer yourselves to God as those brought from death to life, and offer the parts of your bodies to God as weapons of righteousness.
For sin will not rule over you, because you are not under law but under grace.
What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law but under grace? Certainly not!
Do you not know that when you offer yourselves to someone as slaves for obedience, you are slaves of the one you obey, whether of sin leading to death or of obedience leading to righteousness?
But thanks be to God that, though you were slaves of sin, you obeyed from the heart the pattern of teaching to which you were entrusted.
Now, having been freed from sin, serve righteousness.

I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you offered the parts of your bodies as slaves to impurity and lawlessness, leading to lawlessness, so now offer the parts of your bodies as slaves to righteousness, leading to holiness.
For when you were slaves of sin, you were free from righteousness.
What fruit did you have then from the things of which you are now ashamed? For their end is death.
But now, freed from sin and having become servants of God, you have your fruit leading to holiness, and its outcome is eternal life.
For the wages of sin are death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Or do you not know, brothers—for I am speaking to those who know the law—that the law rules over a person as long as he lives?
For a married woman is bound by law to her husband while he is alive, but if her husband dies, she is released from the law concerning her husband.

So, while her husband is alive, she is called an adulteress if she becomes another man's wife. But if her husband dies, she is free from the law and is not considered an adulteress if she becomes another man's wife.
In the same way, you too, brothers, died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong to another, to him who was raised from the dead, so that we might bear fruit for God.
For when we were living in the flesh, the sinful passions that came through the law were active in our bodily members, making us bear fruit for death.
But now we have been released from the law, because we died to that which held us captive, so that we serve in the newness of the Spirit and not in the oldness of the written letter.
What, then, shall we say? Is the law sin? Certainly not! Yet I would not have known sin except through the law, and I would not have recognized coveting if the law had not said, “Do not covet.”
But sin took the opportunity through the commandment and produced every kind of coveting in me. For apart from the law, sin was dead.
I was once alive apart from the law, but when the commandment came to me, sin came to life.
And I died, and the very commandment that was meant for life proved to bring me death.
For sin took the opportunity through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed me.
So the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.

Did what is good, then, become death for me? Certainly not! Rather, it was sin, so that sin might be revealed as sin by producing death in me through what is good, and so that through the commandment sin might become exceedingly sinful.
I know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, sold under sin.
For I do not understand what I do. I do not do what I want, but I do what I hate.
But if I do what I do not want, I acknowledge that the law is good.
Now, however, it is not I who do it, but sin dwelling in me.
I know that nothing good dwells in me—that is, in my flesh. For the desire is present with me, but the ability to do what is good is not.
For I do not do the good that I want, but I do the evil that I do not want.
But if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but sin dwelling in me.
So I find this law: when I wish to do good [?], evil is present with me.
I delight in the law of God according to my inner person.
But I see another law in my bodily members, waging war against the law of my mind and taking me captive through the law of sin that is in my bodily members.
I am a wretched man! Who will rescue me from this body of death?
But thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then, I myself serve the law of God with my mind, but the law of sin with my flesh.
If that is so, there is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has freed me from the law of sin and death.
For what the law could not do, because it was weakened by the flesh, God did by sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, and he condemned sin there in the flesh,
so that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.
For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, and those who live according to the Spirit on the things of the Spirit.
For the mind set on the flesh is death, but the mind set on the Spirit is life and peace.
For the mind set on the flesh is hostile to God, because it does not submit to the law of God, nor indeed can it.
For those who are in the flesh cannot please God.
But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, that person does not belong to him.
But if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is alive because of righteousness.
If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, then he who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit dwelling in you.
From now on, brothers, we are debtors, but not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh.
For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put the deeds of the body to death, you will live.
For those who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.
For you did not receive a spirit of slavery leading back into fear, but you received a spirit of adoption, by which we cry out, “Abba, Father!”
The Spirit himself bears witness to our spirit that we are children of God.
And if we are children, then we are also heirs—heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ. If we share in his sufferings, we shall also share in his glory.
It seems to me that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory to come that will be revealed in us.
For creation waits with eager expectation for the revealing of the sons of God.
For creation was subjected to futility, not by its own will, but because of him who subjected it, in hope
that creation itself has also been freed from slavery to decay into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.
For we know that all creation groans and suffers labor pains together until now.
And not only this, but we ourselves, who have the fruit of the Spirit, groan within ourselves, waiting for adoption, the redemption of our body.
For we were saved in hope. But hope that is seen is not hope, for why would anyone still hope for what they see?
But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it patiently.
Likewise, the Spirit also comes to the aid of our weakness, for we do not know what to pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes with wordless groans.
But he who searches hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to God’s will.
But we know that all things work together for good for those who love God, who were called according to his purpose.
For those whom he knew beforehand he also appointed beforehand to be conformed to the image of his Son, so that he might be the firstborn among many brothers.
And those whom he appointed beforehand he also called; those whom he called he also justified; and those whom he justified he also glorified.
What then shall we say about this? If God is on our side, who can be against us?
He who did not spare his own Son but handed him over for us all—how will he not also graciously give us everything along with him?
Who will bring an accusation against God's chosen ones? It is God who justifies.
Who then will condemn? Christ Jesus is the one who died, and more than that, has risen and is at God's right hand, and indeed intercedes for us.
Who then will separate us from the love of Christ? Affliction, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or suffering, or the sword?
As it is also written: “For your sake we are put to death all day long; we are counted as sheep for slaughter.”
But in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.
For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor rulers, neither things present nor things to come, nor powers,
nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing can separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
I speak the truth in Christ and do not lie; my conscience bears witness with me in the Holy Spirit
that I have great sorrow and unceasing pain in my heart.
For I would pray with vows that I myself might be accursed and separated from Christ for the sake of my brothers and my relatives according to the flesh,
who are Israelites. The adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the worship, and the promises belong to them.
The patriarchs belong to them, and from them came Christ according to the flesh, who is God over all, blessed forever. Amen.
It is not possible that the word of God has failed, for not all who descend from Israel are Israelites.
Nor are all Abraham's descendants his children, but: “Through Isaac your descendants will be named.”
That is, it is not the children of the flesh who are children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as descendants.
For this is the word of promise: “At this time I will come, and Sarah will have a son.”
And not only that, but also in Rebecca's case, through one union with Isaac our father.
For before they were born and before they had done anything good or evil, so that God's purpose according to election might stand—
not from works but from the one who calls—she was told:
“The older will serve the younger,” just as it is also written: “I loved Jacob, but I hated Esau.”
What then shall we say? Is there injustice with God? Certainly not!
For he says to Moses, “I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.”
So it does not depend on the one who wills or the one who runs, but on God, who has mercy.
For Scripture says to Pharaoh, “For this reason I raised you up: to show my power in you, and so that my name might be proclaimed throughout the whole earth.”
So then he has mercy on whom he wishes, and he hardens whom he wishes.
Now you will say, “Why does he still blame us? For no one stands against his will.”
But who are you, a human being, to answer back to God? Will what is created say to its creator, “Why did you make me this way?”
Does the potter not have authority over the clay, to make from the same lump one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?
But what if God, wishing to show his wrath and make his power known, bears with great patience the vessels of wrath prepared for destruction,
so that he might make known the greatness of his glory upon the vessels of mercy, which he prepared for glory?
He also called us, not only from among the Jews but also from among the Gentiles.
As he also says in Hosea, “I will call those who were not my people my people, and her who was not loved beloved.”
And it shall be that in the place where it was said to them, “You are not my people,” there they shall be called children of the living God.
Isaiah cries out concerning Israel, “Even if the number of the children of Israel is like the sand of the sea, only a small remnant will remain.”
For a word brief and concise in righteousness—the Lord will make the word brief upon the earth.
And as Isaiah says, “If the Lord of hosts had not left us offspring, we would have become like Sodom and resembled Gomorrah.”
What then shall we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, attained righteousness—the righteousness that comes from faith.
But Israel pursued the law of righteousness and did not attain the law of righteousness.
Why? Because they pursued it not by faith, but as though by works of the law. For they stumbled against the stumbling stone,
as it is also written, “Behold, I am laying in Zion a stumbling stone and a rock that causes people to fall, and everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame.”
My brothers, my heart’s desire and my prayer to God for them are for their salvation.
For I testify that they have zeal for God, but not with knowledge.
For they are ignorant of God’s righteousness and seek to establish their own, because they did not submit to God’s righteousness.
For Christ is the culmination of the law, bringing righteousness to everyone who believes.
Moses writes about the righteousness that comes from the law: “If a person does it, he will live by it.”
But concerning the righteousness that comes from faith, he says this: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’”—that is, to bring Christ down—
“or, ‘Who will descend into the abyss?’”—that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.
But what does Scripture say? “The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart.” That is the word of faith that we proclaim.
For if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
For with your hearts you believe and are made righteous, and with your mouths you confess and are saved.
For Scripture says, “Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame.”
For there is no distinction between Jew and Gentile, since the same Lord is Lord of all, generous to all who call upon him.
For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.
But how will they call on him in whom they have not believed? Or how will they believe in him whom they have not heard? Or how will they hear without someone preaching?
Or how will they preach unless they are sent? As it is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring the good news of peace and those who bring good news of good things!”
But not everyone obeyed the good news. Isaiah cries out, “Lord, who has believed our report?”
So then, faith comes from hearing, and hearing comes through the word of Christ.
But I ask, did they not hear? Indeed they did: “Their voice went out through all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.”
But I say, did Israel not know? First Moses says, “I will make you jealous through a people that is no people, and through a foolish nation I will provoke you to anger.”
But Isaiah speaks boldly and says, “I was found by those who did not seek me; I revealed myself to those who did not ask about me.”
But concerning Israel he says, “All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and defiant people.”
Now I ask, has God rejected his people? Certainly not! For I too am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
God has not rejected his people, whom he knew beforehand. Do you not know what Scripture says about Elijah, how he brings an accusation before God against Israel?
“Lord, they have killed your prophets and torn down your altars. I alone am left, and they seek my life.”
But what does the answer say to him? “I have kept for myself,” he says, “seven thousand men who have not bent the knee to Baal.”
In the same way, at this present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.
But if it is by grace, it is no longer by works; otherwise, grace is no longer grace.
Now Israel did not obtain what it was seeking, but the chosen obtained it, and the rest were blinded.
As it is written, “God gave them a spirit of foolishness, eyes that would not see and ears that would not hear, down to this very day.”
And David says, “Let their tables become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a punishment for them.
Let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and keep their backs bent forever.”
Now I ask, did they stumble so that they might fall? Certainly not! Rather, through their trespass salvation has come to the Gentiles, to make them jealous.
But if their trespass means riches for the world, and their failure means riches for the Gentiles, how much more will their fullness mean!
But I am speaking to you Gentiles. As long as I am an apostle to the Gentiles, I honor my ministry,
so that perhaps I may make those of my own flesh jealous and save some of them.
For if their rejection means reconciliation for the world, what will their acceptance mean but life from the dead?
If the first portion is holy, so is the whole batch of dough; and if the root is holy, so are the branches.
If some of the branches were broken off, and you, though a wild olive tree, were grafted in among them and came to share in the root and richness of the olive tree,
do not boast over the branches. But if you do boast, remember that you do not support the root; the root supports you.
Now you will say, “The branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.”
That is true. They were broken off because of unbelief, and you stand firm through faith. Do not be proud, but be afraid.
For if God did not spare the natural branches, perhaps he will not spare you either.
Consider, then, God's kindness and severity: severity toward those who fell, but God's kindness toward you, if you remain in that kindness. Otherwise, you too will be cut off.
And they too, if they do not remain in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

For if you were cut from an olive tree that is wild by nature and, contrary to your nature, were grafted into a cultivated olive tree, how much more will those who are its natural branches be grafted into their own olive tree!
Brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, so that you will not be wise in your own eyes: blindness has come upon part of Israel until the full number of the Gentiles comes in.
And then all Israel will be saved, as it is written: “The Savior will come from Zion and turn ungodliness away from Jacob.”
“And this is my covenant with them, when I take away their sins.”
As regards the gospel, they are enemies for your sake; but as regards election, they are beloved for the sake of the fathers.
For God does not revoke his gifts or his calling.
For just as you were once disobedient to God but have now received mercy through their disobedience,
so they too have now become disobedient, so that through the mercy shown to you they too may receive mercy.
For God has confined everyone in disobedience so that he may have mercy on everyone.
Oh, the depth of God's greatness and wisdom and knowledge! How unsearchable are his judgments, and how untraceable his ways!
For who has known the mind of the Lord, or who has become his counselor?
Or who has given him a loan and will receive repayment from him?
For all things are from him and through him and to him. To him be glory forever. Amen.
I appeal to you, brothers, by God's mercies, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God—your rational worship.

And do not conform yourselves to the pattern of this world, but be renewed through the renewal of your minds, so that you may discern what is good and what is the will of God—what is good, pleasing, and perfect.

By the grace of God given to me, I say to everyone among you: do not think more highly of yourself than you ought to think, but think soberly, each according to the measure of faith that God has allotted.
For just as we have many members in one body, and not all the members have the same function,
Likewise, we who are many are one body in Christ, and individually we are members of one another.
But we have gifts of different kinds according to the grace given to us: if prophecy, according to the measure of faith;
if service, according to the service; if someone teaches, according to the teaching;
if someone encourages, according to the encouragement; whoever gives generously, with cheerfulness; whoever oversees, with diligence; whoever shows mercy, with earnestness.
Let love be without hypocrisy. Hate evil and pursue what is good.
Be affectionate toward one another in brotherly love; outdo one another in showing honor.
Do not be timid in your diligence; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord.
Rejoice in hope; endure suffering; persist in prayer.
Share in meeting the needs of the saints; pursue hospitality.
Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
Be of the same mind toward one another. Do not be arrogant, but associate with the humble. Do not be wise in your own eyes.
Repay no one evil for evil. Take thought for what is good in the sight of everyone.
If it is at all possible for you, maintain peace with everyone.
Do not seek revenge for yourselves, beloved, but leave room for wrath, for it is written: “Vengeance is mine, and I will repay, says the Lord.”
But if your enemy is hungry, give him bread, and if he is thirsty, give him water. By doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head.
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
Let every person who is under authority remain in submission, for authority comes from nowhere except from God, and the authorities that exist have been appointed by God.
Therefore, whoever opposes authority opposes God's command, and those who oppose it bring judgment upon themselves.
For rulers are not a terror to good deeds, but to evil deeds. Do you wish not to fear authority? Do what is good, and you will receive praise from it.
For it is God's servant for your good. But if you do evil, be afraid, for it does not bear the sword at its side in vain. It is God's servant, an avenger who brings wrath upon whoever does evil.
Therefore it is necessary to submit, not only because of wrath but also because of conscience.
For this reason you also pay taxes, for they are God's servants, devoted to this very work.
Therefore, pay each person what is owed: taxes to whom taxes are owed, customs duties to whom customs duties are owed, fear to whom fear is owed, and honor to whom honor is owed.
And owe no one anything except to love one another, for whoever loves his neighbor fulfills the law.

“You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not bear false witness,” “You shall not covet,” and any other commandment are summed up in this saying: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
Love does no harm to one's neighbor; love is the fulfillment of the law.
And know this concerning the time: it is now the very hour for us to wake from sleep, for salvation is nearer to us now than when we first believed.
The night has passed, and the day has drawn near. So let us now cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light.
Let us conduct ourselves soberly, as in the daytime, not in revelry and drunkenness, not in promiscuity and impurity, and not in jealousy and strife.
Instead, put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not provide for the flesh to satisfy its desires.
Accept the one who is weak in faith, without passing judgment on their doubts.
One person believes he may eat anything, while the one who is weak eats vegetables.
The one who eats must not despise the one who does not eat, and the one who does not eat must not judge the one who eats, because God has accepted him.
Who are you to judge someone else's servant? Before his own master he stands or falls. But he will stand, because the Lord is able to make him stand.
One person observes one day rather than another, while another observes every day. Let each person be fully convinced in his own mind.

The one who regards the day regards it for the Lord, and the one who does not regard the day does not regard it for the Lord. The one who eats eats for the Lord and gives thanks to God, and the one who does not eat abstains for the Lord and gives thanks to God.
For none of us lives for himself, and none dies for himself.
If we live, we live for the Lord, and if we die, we die for the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
For this very purpose Christ died and lived: to be Lord of both the dead and the living.
Why do you judge your brother? Or why do you despise your brother? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.
For it is written: “As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will acknowledge God.”
So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.
Let us therefore no longer judge one another. Instead, resolve not to put a stumbling block in your brother's way.
I know and am convinced in Christ Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if someone considers something unclean, it is unclean for him.
But if your brother is distressed because of food, you are no longer walking in love. Do not destroy by your food the one for whom Christ died.
Do not let your good be spoken of as evil.
For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by people.
So let us now pursue peace and the things that build one another up.
Do not tear down God's work for the sake of food. Everything is clean, but it is wrong for a person to eat with a troubled conscience.
It is good not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything by which your brother is caused to stumble, falls, or becomes weak.
You indeed have faith; keep it to yourself before God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he uses to test his neighbor.
But the one whose conscience is troubled is condemned even if he eats, because it is not according to faith. For everything that is not from faith is sin.
Now to him who is able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery kept silent through the ages.

and now revealed through the prophetic writings, according to the command of the eternal God, and made known to all nations for the obedience of faith—to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever. Amen.
We who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak and not please only ourselves.
Rather, let each of us please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.
For Christ did not please himself, but, as it is written, “The insults of those who insult you fell upon me.”
Whatever was written was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures we might receive hope.
May the God of endurance and all encouragement grant you to think alike with one another, in accordance with Jesus Christ,
so that in harmony, with one voice, you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore welcome one another, just as Christ welcomed you, to the glory of God.
I say that Christ became a servant of the circumcised for the sake of God's truth, to confirm the promises to the fathers.
But the Gentiles glorify God for his mercy, as it is written: “For this reason I will give thanks to you among the Gentiles and sing psalms to your name.”
And again he says, “Rejoice, Gentiles, with his people.”
And again, “Bless the Lord, all you Gentiles, and praise him, all you peoples.”
And again Isaiah says, “There will be the root of Jesse, and the one who will rise to rule the Gentiles; in him the Gentiles will hope.”
May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace, so that you may abound in hope through the power of the Holy Spirit.
I myself am convinced about you, my brothers, that you too are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, and able to instruct one another.
But I have written somewhat more boldly to you, brothers, as a reminder to you, because of the grace given to me by God,
to be a minister of Jesus Christ among the Gentiles, to make the gospel of God [?], so that the offering of the Gentiles may be acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
Therefore I have reason to boast in Christ Jesus concerning the things of God.
For I dare not speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me to bring the Gentiles to obedience, by words and deeds,
by the power of signs and wonders, by the power of the Holy Spirit, so that from Jerusalem and around as far as the regions of Illyricum I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.
Thus I have been eager to preach the gospel, not where Christ has already been named, so that I might not build upon another person's foundation, but as it is written:
“Those who were not told about him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”
For this reason I have often been prevented from coming to you.
But now I no longer have a place in these regions, and for many years I have had a great longing to come to you.
When I travel to Spain, I hope to see you on my way to them and to be sent onward there by you, after first enjoying your company for a little while.
But now I am going to Jerusalem to serve the saints.
For the Macedonians and the Achaeans were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints who are in Jerusalem.
For they were pleased to do this, and indeed they are indebted to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual blessings, they also owe it to them to share their material goods.
So, when I have completed this and sealed this contribution for them, I will come to you [?] on my way to Spain.
I know that when I come to you, I will come with the fullness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ.
I urge you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to join me in struggling in prayers to God on my behalf,
so that I may be rescued from the disobedient people in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints,
so that, coming to you with joy by God's will, I may find rest with you.
May the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
I commend to you our sister Phoebe, who is a servant of the church in Cenchreae.
Receive her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her in whatever matters she needs and calls on you for, for she herself has assisted many people, including me personally.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
who risked their own necks for my life. Not only I thank them, but also all the churches of the Gentiles.
And greet the church in their house. Greet my beloved Epaenetus, who is the first fruit of Asia for Christ.
Greet Mary, who worked very hard among you.
Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and fellow prisoners, who are outstanding among the apostles and were in Christ before me.
Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
Greet Urbanus, my fellow worker in the Lord, and my beloved Stachys.
Greet Apelles, who is approved in the Lord.
Greet those of the household of Aristobulus. Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet those of the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
Greet Tryphosa and Tryphena, who labor in the Lord. Greet the beloved Persis, who worked very hard in the Lord.
Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who is also mine.
Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brothers who are with them.
Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.
I urge you, brothers, to take note of those who cause divisions and stumbling blocks contrary to the teaching you learned, and avoid them.
For such people do not serve our Lord Christ, but their own bellies, and through smooth talk and flattering praise they deceive the hearts of the innocent.
For word of your obedience has reached everyone, and so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise in what is good and innocent in what is evil.
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
Timothy, my brother and fellow worker, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.
I too, Tertius, who wrote this letter, greet you in the Lord.
Gaius, who is host to me and to the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the city administrator, and Quartus, our brother, greet you.
Now to him who is able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery kept silent through the ages.
and now revealed through the prophetic writings, according to the command of the eternal God, and made known to all the Gentiles for obedience to the faith
To the only wise God, through Jesus Christ—to him be glory forever. Amen.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. To the Romans: written from Corinth through Phoebe the deacon.
